scenario.description: An environmental compliance manager must authorize the offsite shipment of eight drums of spent solvent from a coatings plant and finalize the waste classification, container preparation, segregation, and carrier schedule, with input from a laboratory analyst, a waste logistics coordinator, a maintenance technician, and a production supervisor.

shared_context.S1: Eight drums of spent solvent from the coatings area are staged for disposition and have not yet been released for shipment.
shared_context.S2: The approved waste contractor is available to receive the drums during the current workweek.
shared_context.S3: Mara signs the final shipment authorization and the accompanying waste paperwork.
shared_context.S4: Company procedure requires a pre-shipment review with laboratory, waste logistics, maintenance, and production before Mara signs the authorization.

PF1.text: Leon tested a representative sample yesterday and recorded a 54°C flash point; the current waste profile therefore requires the shipment to be documented as waste code D001 and transported as UN1993, flammable liquid, n.o.s., Packing Group III. He completed the lab worksheet, but it has not yet been attached to the waste file.

PF2.text: Priya confirmed with the contractor this morning that all eight drums can be collected on Friday if the manifest is sent by 14:00 Thursday; the confirmation remains in her email and has not been entered in the shipping calendar.

PF3.text: Gabe inspected the staged containers and found that drums 3 and 6 have damaged bung threads; each must be placed in a UN-rated overpack before loading. He noted the finding on his inspection sheet, but the maintenance system has not been updated.

PF4.text: Sofia's batch records show that drums 7 and 8 contain residual isocyanate catalyst from a separate coating formulation; production's handling instruction requires those two drums to travel on a separate pallet with the catalyst-residue notation. She has retained the batch records for the shift closeout and has not sent them to compliance.

acceptance_conditions: The shipment must either be authorized for all eight drums or deferred with zero drums shipped while the review commitments are completed.
The waste paperwork must use waste code D001 and the transport description UN1993, flammable liquid, n.o.s., Packing Group III, allowing the common punctuation-free variant.
The contractor pickup must be scheduled for Friday and the manifest must be sent by 14:00 Thursday.
Drums 3 and 6 must be placed in overpacks, for a total of exactly two overpacked drums.
Drums 7 and 8 must travel on a separate pallet with the catalyst-residue control recorded.
The lab classification must be cited as justification.

content_checks.C1: (decisions['shipment_authorized'] == True and decisions['drums_shipped'] == 8) or (decisions['shipment_authorized'] == False and decisions['drums_shipped'] == 0 and len(commitments) > 0)
content_checks.C2: decisions['waste_code'] == 'D001' and decisions['transport_description'] in ['UN1993, flammable liquid, n.o.s., Packing Group III', 'UN1993, flammable liquid n.o.s., Packing Group III']
content_checks.C3: decisions['pickup_day'] == 'Friday' and 'Thursday' in decisions['manifest_sent_by'] and '14:00' in decisions['manifest_sent_by']

decisive_facts.why: The 54°C test result changes the paperwork from an unspecified solvent profile to exact waste code D001 and transport description UN1993, flammable liquid, n.o.s., Packing Group III.
The contractor's Friday confirmation changes the schedule to a Friday pickup with the manifest sent by exactly 14:00 Thursday.
The damaged bung threads on drums 3 and 6 change container preparation to exactly two required overpacks.
The catalyst residue in drums 7 and 8 changes loading from one undifferentiated shipment to a separate-pallet arrangement with the catalyst-residue control recorded.
